correctness.rationale: Central symmetry gives W=2h. The radius-a ball is included, and au for U_z≠0 strictly satisfies both cylinder inequalities, so all and only equatorial directions minimize. For (x,y) in the smaller disk, the z contribution is |s|sqrt(b²−y²). Its Lipschitz perturbation of the objective at the equatorial optimizer av is bounded by L|s||q−av|, against a support loss at least sqrt(1−s²)|q−av|²/(2a). Completing the square gives h=a+|s|g(θ)+O_{a,b}(s²) uniformly. Compact separation off the equator and min g>0 imply |s|=O(ε); the event and the strip |s|≤ε/(2g) differ in spherical measure by O(ε²). Integrating dθ ds/(4π) establishes the claimed slope; on that strip the mark change of variables gives the product law with azimuth proportional to 1/g. The slope is strictly decreasing from infinity to zero at fixed a by its positive integral expression, which also verifies the inverse. The stated equal-radius comparator agrees with maximizing (|u_x|+|u_z|)sqrt(a²−y²)+u_y y and the small-product log law localized near ±e_y.
residual_risks: Frozen finite numerical assertions are diagnostic, not all-parameter proof; no fresh run or formal attestation.
